newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads fall 3.9 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian ANZ job ads fall 3.9 pct in Dec.

text.p: The Australian and New Zealand Banking Group said that its job advertisement series for December fell a seasonally adjusted 3.9 percent, more than erasing the 2.1 percent increase recorded in November.
The number of job advertisements in December was 13.8 percent below that of a year earlier, and the lowest number for any month since January 1994, it said.

In trend terms, job ads fell by 0.7 percent last month, after a revised 0.9 percent decline in November, although this still represents an improvement from the middle months of 1996 when job ads were declining by 1.6 and 2.0 percent per month.

"The renewed decline in job ads in December suggests that the demand for labour remains sluggish. As we said last month, it would have been premature to interpret November's increase as a clear signal of a turning point in labour demand," said Saul Eslake, ANZ chief economist.
"However, December's decline in the number of job ads should also be interpreted cautiously, as the series is traditionally very volatile around the holiday period," he added.
The level of job advertising is typically much lower in December than in other months.

The change in seasonally adjusted job ads between November and December overstates the weakness (or understates the strength) in labour demand in those years when Christmas Day falls mid-week (such as 1996), and conversely when Christmas Day falls on a weekend, and especially on a Saturday, ANZ said.
